selected_mechanism.name: ADNR State-Land Disposal Gate for the Stak Energy North Slope AI Data-Center Lease
selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: The Alaska DNR state-land disposal machinery — DMLW lease-application intake, the director's written best-interest finding and public comment, the Final Finding and Decision requiring Commissioner consent, and Commissioner reconsideration on appeal — that controls whether Stak Energy gets 50-year tenure on North Slope state land for a data center and power plant.

news_trigger.quote: More than 500 public comments were received before a preliminary deadline set by the Alaska Department of Natural Resources.
news_trigger.outlet: Copper River Country Journal / Northcountry News

layers.layer: Lease-application intake and administration (50-year lease of North Slope state land)
layers.controlling_actor: DNR Division of Mining, Land & Water (DMLW) leasing program, under AS 38.05.070/.073/.075
layers.what_it_does: DMLW receives and administers Stak Energy's application for a limited property right (lease) on state land; 'A lease is a limited property right on state lands, granted by the Division of Mining, Land & Water (DMLW).'

layers.layer: Written best-interest finding + public notice and comment (min 30 days; extended to July 17, 2026 after 500+ comments)
layers.controlling_actor: DMLW Director, making the written best-interest finding under AS 38.05.035(e)
layers.what_it_does: Statute requires that 'Upon a written finding that the interests of the state will be best served, the director may... approve contracts for the sale, lease, or other disposal'; the public comment period on this finding is the layer the 500+ comments and July 17 extension attach to.

layers.layer: Final Finding and Decision requiring Commissioner consent (CHOKEPOINT)
layers.controlling_actor: Commissioner of Natural Resources (consent power under AS 38.05.035(e); final authority for transactions above the rental threshold)
layers.what_it_does: The director may approve the lease only 'with the consent of the commissioner,' and the commissioner retains approval power for transactions exceeding the $5,000 annual-rental threshold — meaning the commissioner holds final authority over a 50-year industrial lease of this magnitude.
'State statutes require a 20-day appeal period for the applicant and previous commenters, which is followed by a 10-day reconsideration period for the DNR Commissioner.'

chokepoint.layer: Commissioner consent to the Final Finding and Decision (Layer 3)
chokepoint.controlling_actor: Commissioner of the Alaska Department of Natural Resources
chokepoint.binary_decision: Consent to / withhold consent from the 50-year lease disposal
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: AS 38.05.035(e) makes the director's approval conditional on the commissioner's consent, and vests the commissioner with final authority for transactions above the rental threshold. This is one statutory officer, not a committee or board — a single approve/deny gate over the entire lease. The role is institutional and survives any change of incumbent, so the mechanism is not a personality profile (the Stak-CSO/former-commissioner revolving-door detail is context, not the chokepoint).

selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Facilities/power: whether Stak Energy secures 50-year tenure on North Slope state land for a proposed data center and power plant turns on the DNR Commissioner's consent to the DMLW Final Finding and Decision after the July 17, 2026 comment close — the near-term gate that determines the project's ability to proceed and sets precedent for state-land disposal to hyperscale AI development on the Slope.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: This is a classic asymmetric state-land chokepoint: a project with statewide economic and precedent-setting stakes reduces to whether a single cabinet officer signs off on a best-interest finding. The 500+ opposing comments do not decide the outcome — they are input to a finding the commissioner can consent to or not. The revolving-door optics (Stak's chief strategy officer John Boyle was DNR commissioner 2023-2025, now seeking a lease from his former agency) are real and worth flagging, but they do not change the machinery: the same AS 38.05.035(e) consent gate exists regardless of who holds either chair.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Anyone with exposure to North Slope siting, Interior/Slope power, or state-land AI precedent should treat the DNR Commissioner's post-July-17 decision on the Stak best-interest finding as the binding date — not the comment volume. Position around the FFD and the subsequent 20-day appeal / 10-day reconsideration window, which is where the disposal can still be reopened.
